title: What the Reconstruction Engine is
description: The engine rebuilds lost or damaged information from what survived: quotations in other works, redundant copies, earlier versions, and derived artifacts. It produces the most defensible reconstruction possible and marks every uncertain passage, so readers always know which parts are solid and which are educated inference.

title: Consensus reconstruction algorithm
description: Where multiple traces cover the same passage, the engine builds consensus: agreement strengthens confidence, disagreement is preserved as variants rather than averaged away. A passage quoted three ways appears with all three readings and the evidence for each — the reader decides, informed.

title: Failure modes: invented certainty and trace poisoning
description: The worst failures are silent: an engine that fills gaps with plausible invention, or traces planted to rewrite history. Defenses include the schema-level ban on unmarked invention, independence analysis that discounts coordinated traces, and calibration audits that punish overconfidence. Uncertainty is a safety feature.
